book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook opens with the definition of BoP and its format. Here the video starts from the need: buying from abroad costs foreign currency and selling earns it, so a country must keep a reserve, and the reserve rises or falls. Only after a long list of dealings is the umbrella name given (BoP statement). Then the format is built top-down as a tree, and the arithmetic is built bottom-up (each head nets to plus or minus, heads add to account balances, accounts add to BoP). The end returns to the reserve from the first minute, so the whole format is framed as 'what decides whether the vault fills or empties', and the crisis is the vault running dry.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: Follow the foreign currency: first why it moves, then where it is kept, then how every movement is recorded and added up, and finally what the total does to the reserve.

moves.concept: double entry and plus/minus per head
moves.what: RBI records every dealing under each head on both debit and credit sides; this practice is double entry bookkeeping.

moves.concept: double entry and plus/minus per head

moves.concept: account balances, CAS/CAD and overall BoP

narration.density: About 25 terms (foreign currency, forex reserve, FDI, FPI, external borrowing, BoP, RBI, IMF format, current and capital account, visibles, balance of trade, invisibles, services, incomes, NFIA, transfers, remittances, investments, loans, external bonds, double entry, debit/credit, CAS, CAD, BoP crisis) in about 350 s, about 4 per minute, but the 137-235 s stretch packs about 15 of them into 100 s. The first two minutes are comfortable (one idea, one reason at a time); the format part is too fast for a first look and fits revision better.

talmel_summary: The first 140 s (the import/export loop, the vault and the BoP document) produced no tiles because the globe spins non-stop, so the change detector saw one long change; the card says that part fits well (goods and dollars move opposite ways). In the tree part the picture mostly names terms 1-3 s before the voice, as labels and bullets, which is quick to follow but carries no meaning by itself. The strongest fits are in the arithmetic: debit/credit boards under each leaf, arrows down to plus/minus, frames grouping heads into account totals, and the plus/minus wired into the vault; the end is weakened by a promo banner over the crisis moment.

voice.notes: About 198 words per minute, the fastest of this batch; even, explanatory tone with no long pauses. Builds sentences as chains ('aur isi tarah', 'to', 'isliye'), and expands every short form at once (BoP, BoT, NFIA, CAS, CAD). Stress falls on the rule words 'yaad rakhiye' (principal vs interest) and 'soch ke dekhiye' (crisis). No numbers are read anywhere; positive and negative are said as words.

game_ideas.player_does: Drags transaction cards (oil import, software export, NRI sends money home, foreign tourist stays in Goa, FDI in a factory, loan from World Bank, interest paid on that loan) onto the leaves of the BoP tree.
game_ideas.process_happens: Each correct card drops into its leaf's debit or credit board and that board's plus/minus updates; the account totals and the vault level move.
game_ideas.win: All cards placed; the tree's totals and the vault match the statement.
game_ideas.lose: Putting loan interest under capital-account loans bounces the card back with the principal-vs-interest rule shown on the two leaves.

game_ideas.player_does: As RBI for one year, approves or delays monthly dealings (big oil import, IT export contract, FPI pulling money out, foreign loan) while watching the forex vault.
game_ideas.process_happens: Dollar bundles flow along the globe-India loop; the vault's lockers fill or empty; at year end the four boards, two account totals and the BoP plus/minus are drawn.
game_ideas.win: Finish the year with the vault never empty.
game_ideas.lose: If a negative BoP is larger than the vault, the lockers empty and the screen names it a BoP crisis.

checks_learned: Constant decorative motion (the spinning globe) must stop during teaching beats; it hid two minutes of changes from the change detector and competes with the step being taught.
A list of dealings that each move money in or out should be drawn as flows into or out of the reserve, with direction, not as a bullet list.
A 'yaad rakhiye' rule that splits one thing two ways (principal vs interest) must show both halves on screen; only the interest half was drawn.
A topic built on plus/minus balances needs at least one small worked number example; this video has none.
Every short form shown on screen (BoT, NFIA, CAS, CAD) must be expanded by the voice at first use (done here; enforce).
A definition side note (BoP crisis) should not appear more than about 3 s before the voice reaches the term, and promo banners must not cover the canvas while the final definition is spoken.
More than about 8 new terms per minute in a classification tree should trigger a split into two scenes or a recap.

teaching_best.why: Need before name: goods in, money out; goods out, money in; so every dealing is in foreign currency, so a reserve is needed, and only then 'forex reserve'.
Summarise then name: a long list of dealings folds into one umbrella label for one year, which becomes the BoP document.
Double entry made concrete: a debit|credit board under every leaf, arrows to plus/minus, then frames adding heads into account totals, bottom-up.
The arc closes on the vault from minute one; the crisis is taught as a what-if about that vault running dry.

teaching_weak.why: The kinds of dealings are listed without saying which way each moves the reserve (remittances in, loan repayment out).
About 15 terms in 100 s as a text tree, with no numbers and no flow direction; the learner gets names, not meaning.
Surplus and deficit are given as labels; no picture or number of 'earned more than spent'.
A promo banner covers the canvas during the crisis question, and there is no recap of the tree or the arithmetic.
